verdict.rationale: Proa's template macro optimizes markup at compile time by validating it and consolidating static HTML. For interactivity, Proa compiles signals and event handlers into a per-island vanilla-JS module that runs on a shared runtime of about 1.3 KB. Together these suggest compiler-generated, fine-grained client updates, but the docs never say how the DOM is updated or that no diffing step exists. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or documentation that DOM updates skip virtual DOM diffing, a description of the island update mechanism (e.g. signal-to-DOM bindings), and independent benchmarks or hands-on corroboration of client-side update performance.
